2. This case is another epitome of willful disregard and disobedience of High Courts directive tantamounting to Contempt of Court. Factual matrixes forming the background of the contempt Rule are as under.- 

 5. As it has been stated that because of filing of the writ petition the Contemner became annoyed, she filed a departmental case against the petitioner being Departmental Case No.3 of 2012 dated 11-6-2012 to take revenge Notice of the case was accordingly served upon the petitioner and the petitioner was asked to show cause within 3 days why he should not be proceeded against in pursuance of the departmental case. Then on 21-6-2012 upon an application filed by the contempt-petitioner in writ petition No.3961 of 2012 a Division Bench presided over by Justice Naima Haider stayed the operation of the said departmental case NO.03/2012 for a period of 6 months. 

 6. Meanwhile the Supreme Court went on vacation from 26-2-2012 to 7-7-2012 and on. The learned Advocate of the petitioner Mr Manzil Murshid on 21-6-2012 issued certificate intimating about the order of staying the operation of the departmental case No.3 of 2012 which was communicated to the Contemner for taking necessary steps. The said lawyer's certificate was received by the Contemner on 24-6-2012 but after receiving the lawyers certificate dated 21-6-2012 she discharged the petitioner from the service on the next date i.e. 25-6-2012 showing absolute disobedience, disrespect and audacious attitude towards the order of this Division which is clearly a contemptuous act on the part of the Contemner for which she is liable to be punished in accordance with law. 

 8. At the time of issuing Rule this Division directed for personal appearance of the Contemnor Shauli Sumon on 19-7-2012 to clarify her position under the circumstances but on that date as she was in abroad could not appear personally. On 14-8-2012 she personally appeared with an application for dispensation of her personal appearance which was not allowed by this court and the case was adjourned till 30-9-2012 with a further direction for her personal appearance on that date. After that she appeared before this Court time and again and this Court directed her to implement the decision of writ petition No. 3961 of 2012. Likewise when finally the said order on 16-1-2013 being not implemented, the date of final adjudication of the case was fixed on 23-1- 2013. 

 9. This is the factual aspect of the case. Now, we need to clarify some important dates considered to be pertinent for the proper adjudication of the case. 

 (b) Departmental case No.3 of 2012 dated 11-6-2012 was initiated against the petitioner. 

 (c) Departmental case No.3 of 2012 was stayed on 21-6-2012 for a period of 6 months. 

 (d) The letter dated 21-6-2012 issued by the learned Advocate for the petitioner Mr. Manzil Murshid informing about the stay of said departmental case was received by the Contemner on 24-7-2012. 

 (e) The Contemner discharged the petitioner on 25-6-2012 in departmental case No.3 of 2012. 

 (f) By Order dated 24-7- 2012 the order of discharge dated 25-6-2012 passed in Departmental case was stayed by a Division Bench presided over by Mr Justice Mamnun Rahman till disposal of the Rule. 

 12. Another face of the case is that the Contemner filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2237 of 2012 before the Appellate Division for staying operation of the impugned order dated 18-4-2012,21-6-2012 passed in Writ Petition No. 3961 of 2012 and the Appellate Division allowed the prayer staying those orders till 17-2-2013 which subsequently on 4-10-2012 was extended for a further period of 2 (two) months and finally the Appellate Division on 15-10-2012 while disposing of the Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 980 of 2012 filed by the present Contemner against an ad-interim order dated 10-7-2012 passed in this Contempt Petition modified the order passed by the Judge in Chamber directing for disposal of the instant Contempt Petition on merit once for all. 

 15. Further Mr Murshid Contends that the Contemner Ms Shauli Shumon in order to delay the hearing time and again engaged new lawyer one after another which is a cunning technique only to delay the case even when the case was finally ready for hearing. Accordingly at first she engaged Advocate Abdul Nur Dulal on 19-7- 2012, then on 13-9-2012 Advocate Nahid Yasmin, on 12-11-2012 Advocate Nurul Islam Sujon and finally she appointed Advocate SM Razaul Karim at the time when this Court fixed the case on 23-1-2013 for final order. 

 16. That being so the only question that calls for consideration in this case is whether the entire gamut of the factual aspect as depicted above portrays a high handed attitude of the Contemner so to say that by her conducts whether she has willfully and deliberately flouted the order of this Division passed in Contempt Petition and also the orders passed in sequel in writ petition No.3961 of 2012 committing Contempt of Court. 

 19. From now on it cannot be said since there is no specific definition of contempt in the Act (as contempt was not defined in the earlier Act) disposal of a case of Contempt of Court with clarity and perfection cannot be done. The new law on the subject now clearly defines what constitutes 'contempt' of Court. 

 20. In the case in hand we have found that the Contemner even after receiving the letter (lawyer's certificate dated 21-6-2012) on 24-6- 2012 discharged the petitioner from his service by order dated 25-6-2012 pursuant to departmental case which was a flagrant disobedience of the order of this Division and indeed tantamounts to contempt of Court. 

 25. In the case of Asharam M Jain vs AT Gifta, AIR 1983 SC 1151 the Indian Supreme Court has, while, considering whether unqualified apology tendered by the contemner should be accepted or not, referred to a few principles for guidance of the Court. While it is necessary to remember that in dealing with a contemner, the Judges should not be hypersensitive where distortions and criticisms overstep the limits, it is at the same time equally important to deflate vulgar denunciation by dignified bearing, condescending indifference and repudiation by judicial rectitude. In stating the predicament in which the Judges function and conduct themselves in discharging the high duties of office. 

 26. In the case of LD Jaikwal vs State of Up, AIR 1984 SC 1374, the Indian Supreme Court observed that "this was a 'paper' apology and the expression of sorrow came from the pen, not form his heart. For, it is one thing to 'say' sorry-it is another to 'feel' sorry". The learned Judge who delivered the judgment observed" We are sorry to say we cannot subscribe to the 'slap-say sorry and forget' school of thought in administration of con- tempt jurisprudence." 

 29. In the case of Abdul Karim vs State reported in 38 DLR (AD) 188 where it has been held that:- 

 "Reference was made to an earlier case decided by itself where the Court had observed that "in considering whether the apology should be accepted or not, a few facts should be taken into consideration." These facts, as mentioned by the court, are: 

 "(i) As to whether the appellant appreciated that his act was within the mischief of contempt; 

 31. We respectfully agree with the settled proposition that simply begging unconditional apology by itself does not purge an action of contempt. Something more is required to be done as it has been decided in several cases. 

 32. At the outset it has been mentioned that this Contempt Petition has an epitome of its own. It has been found that in the month of August by filing affidavit-in-opposition the Contemner made her first appearance in the case and there she tendered unconditional apology for her conduct and assured that she was willing to comply with the further direction of this Division. But even thereafter she did not carry out the repeated directions of this court for implementing the decision in the Writ Petition No.3961 of 2012. This act of deliberate disobedience is absolutely audacious, outrageous and highly contemptuous which cannot be viewed with impunity. Undoubtedly by her conducts she has committed Contempt of Court. Mr Manzil Murshed's submission in this respects menits substance and deserves all the kudos. 

 39. Having receipt of the aforesaid order of Rule and stay, the contemnor respondent became utterly illogical. Then, to take revenge, she filed a departmental case being No. 306 of 2012 against the petitioner under section 3(A) of Government Servant Special Rule, 1979. 

 40. Against the proceeding of the aforesaid departmental case, the petitioner filed an application in the writ petition No. 3961 of 2012 for staying the proceeding of the departmental case till disposal of the Rule. After hearing the petitioner and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, this Division on 21-6-2012 stayed all further proceeding of the departmental Case being No.3 of 2012 dated 11-6-2012 for a period of 6(six) months. 

 47. The petitioner, then filed an application for vacating the said order of stay. Upon hearing the said application, the Appellate Division modified the order of stay and directed to dispose of the Rule on merit as early as possible within 6-12- 2012. Thereafter, the present case was fixed for hearing by this Division on 5-12-2012. 

 50. The case came up in the list for hearing on 23-1-2013, but the contemnor respondent prayed for time and accordingly this Division fixed the next date on 28-1-2013. 

 57. In the present case the appellant committed contempt of Court by her several acts mentioned hereinabove. She ought to have thrown herself at the mercy of the Court as soon as the Rule for contempt was served upon her with a direction to appear before this Division on 19-7- 2012. But the contemnor willfully transgressed this Division's order by not appearing before this Division on 19-7-2012. In view of the circumstances as mentioned above, we find ourselves unable to condone her action which is not only humiliating to this Division's authority it also amounts to clear defiance of the majesty of law. 

 59. We firmly believe that considerations regarding maintenance of the independence of the judiciary, we do not allow the contemnor escape with impunity on the mere tendering of an apology which in any case does not wipe out the mischief. 

 61. In refusing to accept the apology of the contemner Ellis, J observed in the above case- 

 63. It is not the case of the respondent that she misunderstood our order or there is ambiguity therein. Because, in her affidavit-in-opposition she did not say a single word that the court's order was unclear and ambiguous, rather it is the petitioner who tried to complicate the matter. 

 66. After considering the back ground of the case we find Ms. Shauli Shumon guilty of gross contempt of the court for her willful transgression and afore thought brush-off of this Division order dated 21-6-2012, therefore, we do not accept her unqualified apology.
